mechanism: Niacin causes vasodilation and flushing while guanfacine is an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist causing vasoconstriction and hypotension, creating opposing hemodynamic effects that may complicate blood pressure management.
action: Monitor blood pressure closely during concurrent use; niacin-induced vasodilation may counteract guanfacine's antihypertensive effect or cause unpredictable hemodynamic responses.
